post.title: Money dysmorphia: why 64% of millionaires don't feel wealthy
post.ig:
64% of US millionaires don't call themselves wealthy.

Northwestern Mutual's 2025 study (Harris Poll, 4,626 US adults): only 36% of people with $1M+ invested consider themselves wealthy.
Credit Karma's survey of 1,006 US adults (Dec 2023): 29% report "money dysmorphia", 43% of Gen Z and 41% of millennials. It's a popular term, not a clinical diagnosis.
Northwestern Mutual 2024: $778,000 to feel comfortable vs $2.5 million to be wealthy, a $1.72M gap.
Fed SHED (nearly 13,000 adults, Oct 2025): 73% doing at least okay financially.

Sources: Northwestern Mutual Planning & Progress Study 2024 and 2025, Intuit Credit Karma/Qualtrics, Federal Reserve SHED report (May 2026).
News and education, not financial advice.
